sources.title: Jorge Nocedal and Stephen J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed.
sources.locator: Complete 683-page second-edition PDF retrieved and inspected. Chapter 6 §6.1, BFGS updates and implementation, printed pp. 137–143 / PDF pp. 155–161; Chapter 6 §6.4, Assumption 6.1, Theorems 6.5–6.6 and their full proofs, printed pp. 153–160 / PDF pp. 171–178; Chapter 7 §7.2, L-BFGS two-loop recursion and cost, printed pp. 178–179 / PDF pp. 196–197; Chapter 18 §18.3, Powell damping, printed pp. 537–538 / PDF pp. 555–556.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.1: BFGS Hessian and inverse updates, secant equations, and positive definiteness
contents.reason: The item states both direct and inverse updates, their common curvature denominator, secant equations, and Powell damping convention.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.4, Assumptions 6.1–6.2: bounded and uniformly positive Hessian estimates on convex sublevels
contents.reason: The local lemma derives the gradient, monotonicity, and quadratic Taylor estimates from the declared Hessian bounds and proves each estimate in full.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.1: positive-curvature BFGS update preserves positive definiteness
contents.reason: The local proof establishes the direct and inverse secant equations, symmetry, positive definiteness, and reciprocal consistency algebraically.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.1: Wolfe curvature inequality gives a positive BFGS pair
contents.reason: The local proof derives sᵀy ≥ (1−c₂)α|gᵀp| from the Wolfe curvature condition and strict descent.

contents.name: Chapter 18 §18.3, Procedure 18.2: Powell damping and thresholded curvature repair
contents.reason: The local algebra verifies 0<θ<1 in the damped branch and sᵀỹ=0.2sᵀBs>0.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.1: dense Hessian direction solve and factorization-cost comparison
contents.reason: The algorithm specifies the failure-aware Cholesky and triangular-solve path while making no backward-error claim.

contents.name: Chapter 7 §7.2, equations (7.15)–(7.20), Algorithms 7.4–7.5: L-BFGS scaling, two-loop recursion, and limited storage
contents.reason: The carrier defines both loops, scale selection, curvature filtering, finite budgets, and explicit failure returns.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.4, equations (6.42)–(6.51): BFGS trace, determinant, and potential identities
contents.reason: The item derives the trace and determinant update identities and the potential inequality with the SPD and logarithm hypotheses explicit.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.1 and Chapter 18 §18.3: full-memory BFGS update with descent safeguarding and damping
contents.reason: The algorithm fixes exact and rounded direction branches, resets, Wolfe failures, damping, and update statuses.

contents.name: Chapter 7 §7.2, Algorithm 7.4 and cost discussion: two-loop recursion equals sequential inverse updates and costs O(mn)
contents.reason: The local induction proves equality with the stored inverse updates and counts both arithmetic and storage.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.4, Assumption 6.1 and Theorem 6.5 with full proof: global BFGS convergence under uniform convexity
contents.reason: The authored proof states the exact convex-sublevel and Hessian bounds and independently completes the trace-potential and Zoutendijk argument.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.4, trace and determinant estimates: bounded correction pairs imply eigenvalue control
contents.reason: The local proof supplies explicit spectrum constants from trace and determinant bounds for at most m updates.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.4, Assumption 6.2 and Theorem 6.6 with complete Dennis–Moré proof
contents.reason: The assigned lemma proves the Dennis–Moré limit under the exact undamped branch and a locally Lipschitz Hessian.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.4, Theorem 6.6: eventual unit steps and superlinear convergence
contents.reason: The consumer verifies Armijo and strong curvature at the unit trial and deduces the superlinear error ratio.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.4: full-memory and limited-memory results have distinct hypotheses
contents.reason: The L-BFGS theorem states its own fixed-memory pair and scale bounds and does not import the full-memory Dennis–Moré conclusion.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.1: exact secant update on a strongly convex quadratic
contents.reason: The example computes the exact directional minimizer, strong Wolfe tests, update matrix, and secant equation.

contents.name: Chapter 18 §18.3: Powell damping after a negative-curvature trial pair
contents.reason: The example computes the raw indefinite update and the positive definite Powell-damped update, while explicitly rejecting the trial from the Wolfe search.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.1 and Chapter 7 §7.2: dense versus limited-memory storage and work
contents.reason: The example counts entries for n=1000 and m=10 and distinguishes asymptotic work from exact operation totals.

sources.title: Dong C. Liu and Jorge Nocedal, “On the limited memory BFGS method for large scale optimization,” Mathematical Programming 45 (1989), 503–528.
sources.locator: Complete 27-page paper PDF retrieved and inspected. §§2–4, limited-memory updates and recursion, printed pp. 506–516 / PDF pp. 5–15; §6, Algorithm 6.1, correction-pair assumptions, Theorem 6.1 and complete trace/determinant proof, printed pp. 521–526 / PDF pp. 20–25.

contents.name: §2: limited-memory inverse BFGS update and stored correction pairs
contents.reason: The algorithm records the finite-memory state, scale, positive-curvature filter, and two-loop recursion.

contents.name: §§2–4: reverse and forward loop equations and their storage/work purpose
contents.reason: The local proof writes each loop as a BFGS matrix-vector update and counts O(mn) work and storage.

contents.name: §6: correction-pair and initial-scale bounds used in the global convergence proof
contents.reason: The assigned lemma states explicit pair and scale bounds and derives a uniform spectral interval.

contents.name: §6, Algorithm 6.1, Theorem 6.1 and full proof: fixed-memory L-BFGS global convergence
contents.reason: The authored theorem states stronger explicit pair and scale hypotheses and proves a separate linear convex rate.

contents.name: §6, trace/determinant relations (6.10)–(6.13)
contents.reason: The local lemma proves the exact identities used to bound the spectrum and potential.

contents.name: §2 and §6: limited-memory storage and computational cost
contents.reason: The example gives a concrete n=1000, m=10 comparison and states the asymptotic limits.

sources.title: Manuel Carreira-Perpiñán, Lecture Notes on Numerical Optimization.
sources.locator: Complete 98-page lecture-notes PDF retrieved and inspected. §6, BFGS update, positive definiteness and convergence scope, printed pp. 20–23 / PDF pp. 21–24; §7, L-BFGS recursion and cost, printed pp. 25–26 / PDF pp. 26–27.

contents.name: §6: BFGS Hessian/inverse update and secant convention
contents.reason: The local definition fixes the Hessian and inverse update notation and identifies the damped secant vector.

contents.name: §6: Hessian and strong-convexity hypotheses used in BFGS descent and convergence estimates
contents.reason: The independently authored lemma makes the bounded-Hessian implications explicit and proves the required gradient and Taylor bounds.

contents.name: §6: positive curvature and positive-definiteness boundary
contents.reason: The local proof verifies positive definiteness exactly under the positive-curvature hypothesis.

contents.name: §6: full-memory convergence scope and local superlinear boundary
contents.reason: The notes are used as an independent treatment of the uniform-convexity and Hessian hypotheses; the full proof is supplied locally.

contents.name: §7: L-BFGS two-loop recursion and O(mn) cost
contents.reason: The algorithm and equivalence lemma independently spell out the loop order and its cost.

contents.name: §7: limited-memory correction pairs and scaling
contents.reason: The local theorem makes the pair-scale conditions explicit rather than inferring a spectrum from positive curvature alone.
